$comment: What was read, and at which revision, for every column of the comparison table in README.md.
The table is the one thing this project ships that makes claims about other people's software,
and it goes wrong without anything breaking. `npm run smoke` already checks how OLD it is;
this file makes it checkable whether the other side has MOVED since we looked, which is the
question that actually decides whether a cell still holds. `npm run table-sources` compares
each `sha` against that project's current HEAD and names the columns worth re-reading.
Adopted from csitte.at, whose rule is 'no matrix cell without our own evidence' — they record
the foreign HEAD before mirroring a row. On 2026-08-26 their recorded SHA for taylorwilsdon
and ours matched, which is how a claim about a third party should be confirmable at all.
The README's `comparison-table-verified` marker carries the OLDEST `verified` date in this
file, not the newest, and a test enforces exactly that. A table is only as current as its
stalest column; tying the marker to the newest check would let one freshly re-read column
stand in front of the others and — since the age budget in `npm run smoke` is measured from
that same marker — reset the budget for all of them. On 2026-09-07 the taylorwilsdon column
alone moved the marker from 09-03 to 09-07, which is what prompted the rule. So: pulling one
column forward no longer re-dates the table, and the columns that hold the marker back are
named in the test failure.
`shaBasis` is deliberately part of the record: `recorded` means the SHA was read at the time
of checking, `inferred` means it was reconstructed afterwards from the commit history (safe
only when the repository did not move between the check and the reconstruction). Never write
`recorded` for a SHA nobody wrote down — that is the exact habit this file exists to break.

columns.note: Full re-read of the MCP tool reference itself on 2026-09-03 (not the Cloud blog), replacing the 2026-08-31 reading of the same page: still Developer Preview, and the same ten tools by name — create_draft, get_message, get_thread, label_message, label_thread, list_drafts, list_labels, search_threads, unlabel_message, unlabel_thread. No send, no filters, no unsubscribe, no snooze, no query-driven bulk. The page documents no return fields at all, which is why the structured-output and sender-authentication cells both read as not offered / not documented rather than as a denial: nothing there mentions SPF, DKIM, DMARC or Authentication-Results. Every cell in this column checked against that page, not carried over.

Full re-read of all eleven cells on 2026-08-31 at this revision (the 2026-08-29 entry was a delta check; this replaces it). Read gmail/gmail_tools.py end to end: sixteen Gmail tools, send_gmail_message present, no snooze, no unsubscribe action (List-Unsubscribe only appended to the exported message body), search_gmail_messages returns ids and links without re-checking labels, batch_modify_gmail_message_labels takes message_ids — an explicit list, not a query — and defaults verify=True, which reads the labels back. auth/credential_store.py CHANGED A CELL: LocalDirectoryCredentialStore writes with file mode 0600 and no encryption, GCSCredentialStore delegates to bucket-level CMEK with 'no app-level key'. The cell said a plain yes, which read as app-level token encryption like ours; now it names both mechanisms. No output_schema anywhere in the repository. Scope coupling unchanged since 2026-08-26 (auth/scopes.py, main.py). He now also sells a managed instance, which does not change the 'you operate the server' row: self-hosting remains fully supported. 2026-09-03: brought forward from the 2026-08-31 revision by reading the diff rather than the files again — eleven commits, and none of them touches a cell. They are an OAuth client-secret-file fallback (auth/client_secrets.py, auth/oauth_config.py, core/server.py, main.py) and label colours on the existing manage_gmail_label tool (gmail/gmail_tools.py, gmail/gmail_helpers.py); the tool count, the scope model, the storage mechanisms and the absence of output_schema are all untouched. The sender-authentication cell was re-checked at this HEAD directly: GMAIL_METADATA_HEADERS still ends at List-Id (lines 42-44, which is also the control that proves the search works), and Authentication-Results, dkim, dmarc and spf have no hit in the file. A diff that leaves a cell's code identical is a stronger record than reading the same lines twice — but it is a different check, and this note says which one was run. 2026-09-07: brought forward to 54b1c56 (v1.26.0), 43 commits on, and the round was prompted by a gap on our side rather than a move on his. auth/permissions.py has carried `--permissions <service>:<level>` since 2026-02-25 and was last touched 2026-07-30; the 2026-08-26 reading covered only auth/scopes.py and main.py and so recorded the least-privilege cell as though --read-only were the one switch that narrows scopes. Read at this revision: auth/permissions.py (cumulative levels readonly, organize, drafts, send, full; get_scopes_for_tools returns BASE_SCOPES plus the level's scopes and overrides both the full and the read-only map), core/tool_registry.py (a tool whose _required_google_scopes fall outside the level is disabled, explicitly without scope-hierarchy expansion, so organize excludes gmail.send) and auth/scopes.py. The cell and the paragraph under the table now name that second mechanism; what stays a caveat is the direction — the level is picked per service, not derived from the enabled tools — and the absence of a request-level guard. The other ten cells were brought forward by diff rather than re-read: gmail/gmail_tools.py moved +247/-61 without adding or removing a tool (attachment size handling, body format, the forward and draft paths), output_schema still has no occurrence anywhere in the repository, and nothing in the diff touches snooze, an unsubscribe action, label re-verification or Authentication-Results. One diff hunk is worth naming although it changes no cell: auth/service_decorator.py now substitutes the full Drive scope for drive.file under domain-wide delegation, which widens rather than narrows — a Drive path, and outside the Gmail scope of this table. 2026-09-08: one more file read at the same revision, on a point raised by csitte.at rather than found here, and it holds. In core/tool_registry.py the function is filter_server_tools — its docstring, not its name, says it removes disabled tools from the server after registration, which is presumably where the name in their report came from; there is no remove_disabled_tools in the file. The tier filter is block 1 and runs unconditionally; the read-only filter is block 3 and carries an explicit 'and not permissions_mode'; the permissions filter is block 4. All of them add into one tools_to_remove set, and block 4 skipping names already in it spares work rather than changing the outcome. So at the TOOL gate --tool-tier and --permissions add up, and only --read-only is displaced — the mirror image of the scope side, where the permission level overrides both scope maps. The startup log reports a single mode (Permissions wins over Read-Only) even when the tier filter also removed tools, which is worth knowing before quoting that line as evidence. No cell moves: ours names the two effects separately. `verified` deliberately stays 2026-09-07 — this was one file on one point, not a round over the eleven cells, and a date made younger by a touch this small would claim a check nobody ran.

Full re-read of all eleven cells on 2026-08-31 at this revision; SHA now recorded rather than inferred. Fourteen files under src/tools/gmail: sendEmail and sendDraft present, no snooze, no unsubscribe, no filter tools. modifyMessageLabels takes ONE messageId — there is no bulk path at all, by ids or by query. listMessages passes q and labelIds straight to messages.list and returns the labels without checking them against the query. triageInbox does carry heuristic per-message signals (newsletter via List-Unsubscribe, meeting keywords, question mark, action requested) plus aggregate stats, so that cell stands. auth.ts has a fixed SCOPES array — no tiers, no derivation. No outputSchema in the repository. No token encryption: firestoreTokenStorage.ts has no cipher; the AES in downloadProxy.ts is for download links, not tokens. 2026-09-03: brought forward from the 2026-08-31 revision by reading the diff — five commits, none of which touches src/tools/gmail or src/auth.ts. They add a batchApplyTextStyle Docs tool and adjust Drive and Sheets listings; the only shared file they touch is src/types.ts, and the 33 added lines there are the Docs batch-style schema. So every Gmail cell, the fixed SCOPES array and the absence of token encryption stand on the 2026-08-31 reading, unchanged in code. The sender-authentication cell holds for the same reason: no Gmail file moved.

First reading of this column, added on 2026-09-08 — the date we read, at the revision the repository stood at. It was found by a landscape scan rather than by any cell moving, and the finding is about our own selection: at 176 stars it is an order of magnitude larger than the klodr column we already carried, actively maintained, TypeScript, Apache-2.0. It had been passed over because it is a Workspace suite rather than a Gmail server, which is a reason to describe it carefully, not a reason to omit it. Read at this revision: src/factory/manifest/gmail.yaml end to end (fifteen Gmail operations — search, read, archive, send, reply, replyAll, forward, triage, trash, untrash, getAttachment, viewAttachment, modify, labels, threads, getThread — so send, reply and forward are all present), src/factory/safety.ts, src/accounts/credentials.ts, src/server/batch.ts. The send row is the one that made this column worth adding: safety.ts defines a `draft-only-email` policy blocking send/reply/replyAll/forward, and a `no-delete` policy blocking permanent deletion — the only other server on this table that will refuse to send at all. Both are opt-in through GWS_SAFETY_POLICY, so the default is a sending server and the promise is an operator's environment variable, which is why the cell reads `sends` first. Bulk is by explicit ids, not by query: batch.ts maps `users.messages.batchModify` over `items` carrying a messageId (`ids: items.map(...)`), with no query path anywhere. `triage` is a fixed `messages.list` with `q: 'is:unread in:inbox'` plus a per-message hydration walk — a list, with no bucketing or aggregate stats, hence the qualified cell rather than a tick. `search` is `messages.list` with hydration via `messages.get` at format=metadata; the returned labels are never re-checked against the query, so the re-verification cell is a dash. It goes through messages.list rather than threads.list, which is the endpoint our own measurement found the drift in — worth recording, because it means the cell describes a missing check and not an observed failure. No unsubscribe, no snooze, no filter tool: `snooze`, `unsubscribe`, `Authentication-Results`, `dkim` and `dmarc` have no hit in the repository, and the only occurrence of `filter` in gmail.yaml is a comment — `users.settings.filters.*` appears solely in src/google/descriptor.json, which is the generated catalogue of what Google offers, not of what the server registers. No output_schema or outputSchema anywhere. credentials.ts writes the token as plain JSON at mode 0600 with no cipher, so the encryption cell is a dash like the other community columns. The least-privilege cell names something genuinely different from ours and worth watching: ADR-202 records a per-ACCOUNT read/readwrite level, and safety.ts enforces it at call time against the scopes Google actually granted — read from the credential file, checked against Google's own per-method scope list in the generated descriptor rather than a hand-kept table. Its direction is the same as ours; its position is later, at the call rather than at registration. One limitation the file states about itself, which is why our own guard sits where it does: the policy check runs in the factory handler pipeline, so hand-registered tools get none for free — `manage_scratchpad` had to call it explicitly after shipping without it (the comment names this as how scratchpad went uncovered).

Full re-read of all eleven cells on 2026-08-31 at this revision; SHA now recorded rather than inferred. Thirty-five tool names across src/tools/*: send_email, send_draft, reply_all and forward_email present, no snooze, no unsubscribe. batch_modify_emails takes args.messageIds, so bulk is by explicit id list. get_inbox_with_threads passes q to threads.list and returns summaries — no bucketing, no label re-check. The sender-authentication cell was checked at this same revision: no hit for Authentication-Results, dkim, dmarc or spf.
